svg.text: The cross-encoder erases the chunk-size effect on both legs
Paired contrasts in nDCG@10 (marginal means over the overlap rungs, token_window cells only): first-stage dense retrieval, and
the same ranking after bge-reranker-v2-m3. Bars are 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs over the sampling unit. Each leg keeps its own
x-scale and its own pre-registered bar X - the legs' absolute scores are not comparable.
Leg B — PMC OA, 260 queries, ×11.5 rung
dense retrieval — null the design could see
after reranking — null the design could see
A contrast is read as resolved only when its CI excludes zero AND its magnitude clears both the leg's bar X and δ80. On Leg B's deep rung every dense
size contrast resolves and not one of them survives reranking; the shrinkage is itself a resolved effect (size 2048 − 256: dense minus reranked =
−0.0618, CI [−0.0902, −0.0340]), so this is not a power artefact. On Leg A only one dense step resolves (1024 − 512, +0.1204) and it collapses to
+0.0120. That step is the study's one genuine both-legs-resolvable contradiction - and it exists only in front of the reranker that production runs.
Overlap is the one uncontested axis: a null on both legs, adequately powered on both, for a cost of up to 1.32× the vectors (61,559 extra vectors on
5,000 documents at size 256, for a recall@100 change of exactly 0.0000). The overlap rows take each leg's pre-registered primary rung, which for Leg B
is the judged-only ×0 corpus; its ×11.5 replication points the same way (−0.0078) but does not clear the bar.
